methods.name: arca_status
methods.summary: Node status: the API version, the node id, the mode, the uptime, whether Incus answers and the last applied sequence number.

methods.name: node_metrics
methods.summary: Host metrics of the node: the latest sample and the mean over the requested minutes.

methods.name: watch_report
methods.summary: Every instance in every project with its ownership class, and the drift between marks and desired state.

methods.name: token_list
methods.summary: The interim API tokens by id and scope. Never a secret or a hash.

methods.name: journal_list
methods.summary: The newest record for each effect in the journal, paged by effect id. It names only the intent and object fields, never a pre-image or inverse.

methods.name: plan_list
methods.summary: The delete plans and action proposals waiting for an owner's approval. Delete plans carry the exact statement the owner signs; action proposals carry their action, arguments and kernel-built summary.

methods.name: action_propose
methods.summary: Records an inert service, database, GPU assignment, storage, snapshot or instance start, stop or restart action proposal for the owner to approve with a passkey. Nothing changes until the owner approves it.

methods.name: plan_decline
methods.summary: Declines a waiting delete plan. Its objects are retained, and the decline is final.

methods.name: approval_submit

schema.description: Optional. Absent or true: the call runs as without it. False: the call is refused, nothing changes and no approval is spent. It is never part of what an approval binds.

methods.summary: Submits an owner's approval for a waiting delete plan, which deletes the plan's objects once. The approval is never echoed.

methods.name: action_approve

schema.description: Optional. Absent or true: the call runs as without it. False: the call is refused, nothing changes and no approval is spent. It is never part of what an approval binds.

methods.summary: Submits an owner's passkey approval for a waiting action proposal, which runs its action once. The approval is checked by this kernel's own verifier and never echoed; an approval page on the same machine relays a linked host's approvals here.

methods.name: peer_keys_sync
methods.summary: Keeps the owner passkeys of the page host `approval.peerKeys` names, for action approvals only. The first set is kept as is; a changed set needs a passkey approval by a key already kept, and without one the answer is the statement to sign. Lines are never echoed. When `approval.peerKeys` lists several sources, `from` names the page host whose set this is (absent: the first source), and a change needs a key already kept for that same source.

methods.name: alerts_list
methods.summary: The node's alerts: the firing ones, those whose data is unknown, the disabled rules, the recent resolves, and the store's health.

methods.name: postgres_create

schema.description: Filled in by the node: the template a database is made from when its config names no image (postgres-autopg). A caller leaves it out.

Filled in by the node with the template: SHA-256, in hex, of the template's file and of each script it names. The create runs only while the template on the node is still exactly that one. A caller leaves it out.
Always refused. The database verbs act in the node's own project only. Inside a tenant, a database is the postgres service template, created with service_create and linked with service_connect.

methods.summary: Create a Postgres database in the node's service project (arcak-svc). Give the name only: the image is the node's, never the call's. With no kernel.postgresImage in the node's config, the database is a service from the node's postgres-autopg template: its digest-pinned image is fetched, the template generates the password (when it does not, the service is created stopped and stoppedBecause says why), and the answer says service: true; connect to it with service_connect, remove it with service_remove. With kernel.postgresImage, it is a database of the old kind from that image, linked with postgres_link. Returns its name, its entry and the status pending; postgres_list shows when it runs.

methods.name: postgres_list

schema.description: Always refused. The database verbs act in the node's own project only. Inside a tenant, a database is the postgres service template, created with service_create and linked with service_connect.

methods.summary: The Postgres databases in the node's service project (arcak-svc), each with its name, its entry, its status (pending until it has an address), its address, its port and the consumers linked to it. A database made from the node's postgres-autopg template is a service: its row carries service: true, its links are the services connected to it, and the service verbs act on it (service_connect, service_remove). A node with no database answers an empty list. Never a password or a connection URL. A tenant's databases are services: service_list shows them.

methods.name: postgres_link

schema.description: Always refused. The database verbs act in the node's own project only. Inside a tenant, a database is the postgres service template, created with service_create and linked with service_connect.

methods.summary: Link a consumer to a Postgres database: the database's network ACL lets the consumer reach it, and the consumer is given the connection URL under DATABASE_URL for its first database, or DATABASE_URL_<NAME> for each other. Returns the variable names only, never the URL. The consumer is one the node already records (arca probe consumer add); a service is linked with service_connect instead.

methods.name: postgres_unlink

schema.description: Always refused. The database verbs act in the node's own project only. Inside a tenant, a database is the postgres service template, created with service_create and linked with service_connect.

methods.summary: Remove the link between a consumer and a Postgres database: the database's network ACL stops letting the consumer in, and the consumer loses the connection URL it was given. Returns the names of the variables removed. The database and its data stay.

methods.name: postgres_delete

schema.description: Optional. Absent or true: the call runs as without it. False: the call is refused, nothing changes and no approval is spent. It is never part of what an approval binds.
Always refused. The database verbs act in the node's own project only. Inside a tenant, a database is the postgres service template, created with service_create and linked with service_connect.

methods.summary: Delete a Postgres database and its data. The call itself, at once, removes every consumer's link to the database, its password and the connection URLs Arca kept, even when the delete of the database then waits for the owner. Returns removed: true and no plan when the database is gone, or removed: false and the delete plan that waits for the owner's approval (plan_list shows it, approval_submit carries the approval).

methods.name: ontology_query
methods.summary: The ownership, status and outgoing calls for an item in Arca's public ontology.

methods.name: service_create

schema.description: The service name (1-40 of a-z, 0-9 and inner "-", starting with a letter).
The template's name.

For a virtual-machine template: the existing host bridge its NIC joins, one of the node's allowed bridges. Left out, the virtual machine joins the managed service network when the node has one, and otherwise the node's only allowed bridge.

A deploy id: 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9 and "-". What a create inside a tenant makes under it is provisional until the same token confirms the deploy or 15 minutes pass, and that token may roll the deploy back until then.

Only for a service this node's config names in kernel.serviceDestinations: exactly the addresses and tcp ports the config names for it. A proposal made with action_propose fills it in from the config, so the owner's approval binds it and the owner's card shows each address; a caller has no need to state it, and cannot state one of its own. Such a service, and everything that runs in it, can reach each address on its one tcp port through this node; every other private address stays closed. A create of such a service runs only from an approved proposal: called directly it is refused with NotApproved. Refused in a tenant and for a virtual machine on a host bridge.

Filled in by the node when a create is proposed: the image the template names, <image>@sha256:<digest> when it gives a digest and the bare name when it gives none; a virtual machine that names a version adds " running <version>". The owner's card shows it and the approval binds it. A caller leaves it out; one that states it must state the node's own.

Only for a template that declares kernelAccess: the template's own kernelAccess. A proposal made with action_propose fills it in from the template, so the owner's approval binds it and the owner's card says it; a caller has no need to state it. Such a service can call this node's kernel from inside its instance, at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp, with whatever token it is given; the token's scope and tool list decide what it may do. A create of such a template runs only from an approved proposal: called directly it is refused with NotApproved. Refused in a tenant, and on a node that sets no listen.services.
For a virtual-machine template on a host bridge: a fixed MAC for its NIC, six hex octets joined by ":". Left out, Incus picks one. Refused on the managed service network.

Only for an image on a registry this node holds a credential for (registry_secret_set): that registry's address. A proposal made with action_propose fills it in, so the owner's card says that the image is fetched with the credential and that Incus then keeps it with the image; a caller has no need to state it. Such a create runs only from an approved proposal.

For a virtual-machine template that lists createSettings: the settings this one service gets in place of the template's defaults, by name. Only a listed name is taken, and a value has the type of the template's default; an address is a plain https address. Never a secret: service_status shows them. Fixed at create.

Optional. Absent or true: the service is started once it is created, as without the field. A container whose template needs a secret that is not set yet, and a virtual machine whose template declares secrets, are created stopped whatever this says, and the answer's stoppedBecause says why. False: it is created stopped, the answer's state is "stopped", and its create carries no boot.autostart, so a host restart does not boot it before its first instance_start and afterwards restores the state it was in. service_secret_set and service_connect then apply to it, and instance_start starts it for the first time: a container with every secret and link in its environment. A virtual machine's secrets are never in its environment: instance_start writes them into the guest as files once it has booted, in a tenant's machine as in one of the node's own.

Filled in by the node when a create is proposed: SHA-256, in hex, of the template's file and of each script it names, as the node holds them then. The create runs only while the template on the node is still exactly that one. A caller leaves it out; one that states it must state the node's own.
Optional. The tenant to act in: the verb then sees and changes only that tenant's project. Left out, it acts in the node's own project. A node without kernel.tenants has no tenants.

destinations.description: Present only on a service that may reach a private address through this node: each address and the one tcp port open on it, as this node's config (kernel.serviceDestinations) named them when the owner approved the create. Every other private address stays closed to the service. service_status also answers ready for each and, when it is false, problem.

address.description: One IPv4 address in a private range or the tailnet range, outside the service subnet.

port.description: The one tcp port open on that address.

problem.description: service_status only, when ready is false: what does not stand as recorded.

ready.description: service_status only: the network rules Incus holds for the service are the ones its record gives, and the address is not one of the node's own.

ipv4.description: Its fixed address on the service bridge, from its record. A virtual machine on a host bridge takes its address from that network and has none in its record: service_list leaves this empty and sets ipv4In, and service_status reads it from the running machine's live state. Empty with neither ipv4In nor ipv4Problem: it has none now.

ipv4In.description: service_list only, on a virtual machine on a host bridge: its address is not in its record and exists only in its live state, which the list does not read. service_status of it reads it.

ipv4Problem.description: service_status only, on a running virtual machine on a host bridge whose live state could not be read: why, in words. ipv4 is then empty because it was not read, and every other field is as usual.

kernelAccess.description: Present only on a service whose template declares kernelAccess: the service can call this node's kernel from inside its instance, at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp, with whatever token it is given. service_status also answers ready and, when it is false, problem.

connect.description: The path of the socket on the host its device connects to: the node's listen.services as it was when the service was created.

port.description: The port inside the instance, on its loopback.

problem.description: service_status only, when ready is false: what does not stand as recorded.

ready.description: service_status only: whether the instance carries the device as Arca made it and this server's listen.services is still the socket it connects to.

lanPort.description: Its host port when the template has a lan proxy, or null.

links.description: The services it is linked to, as a consumer, and the port each link opens.

note.description: Present when there is something to know about how this row was read: on a node that only looks, an instance of the service project that this node holds no record of is shown as it is and marked "not recorded by this node".

ports.description: The ports it listens on; a link opens the first.

published.description: Its dash on the tailnet (service_publish), or null.

state.description: failed: Incus reports an error, or its instance is gone; unknown: an instance droidd did not create, which it leaves alone.

stoppedBecause.description: Present when the service was created stopped: why, in words that name a secret and never show one. Either the call said start: false, or its template is created stopped whatever the call says.

template.description: Its template (empty for an instance droidd did not create).

update.description: The version the service runs beside the one its template, as installed on this node, names now. Both come from this node's own records and files: no registry is asked. service_list carries it only when the two differ, with state alone; service_status carries it for every service whose own version is known (a container made from an image by digest, or a virtual machine whose template names its version's setting in update.pin). Two digests carry no order: differs says the template names another version, never which one is newer. Today the only way to the template's version is service_remove and service_create.

pin.description: service_status only: the version the service was created with, an image by digest.

problem.description: service_status only, when state is unknown: why the installed template cannot say.

state.description: same: the installed template names the version the service runs. differs: it names another one. unknown: the template is not installed any more, cannot be used, or is of another kind now.

templatePin.description: service_status only: the version the installed template names now.

methods.summary: Create a service from a template, in the service project and under the kernel's mark: a container on the service network, or a virtual machine on the service network or on an existing host bridge the node allows. With start: false it is created stopped, so service_secret_set and service_connect put its secrets and links in place before instance_start starts it for the first time.

The function's name (1-40 of a-z, 0-9 and inner "-", starting with a letter). Functions and services share one name space.
When the function runs: exactly one trigger, a timer. A run starts every everySeconds, unless one is still going.
The one-shot grant of the approved action proposal. The owner approves the proposal; this verb is not called with an approval of its own.
The program and its arguments: the first is the program's absolute path inside the image. No shell runs it. Left out, the image's own entry point runs.
How many runs of the function may go at once. This build runs one: the only value is 1, which is also the default.

Only for a function this node's config names in kernel.serviceDestinations: exactly the addresses and tcp ports the config names for it. A proposal fills it in from the config, so the owner's card shows each address and the approval binds it; a caller cannot state one of its own.
Plain environment values, by name, at most 32. The owner's card shows each whole. Never a secret: a secret is named in secrets.
How a run is isolated. This build runs a function in a container: the only value is "container", which is also the default.

What one run may use. seconds: the longest it may take (default 60); Arca stops a run that passes it, with a stop the program has 5 seconds to obey and then a kill. memory: the most it may use, as a size such as 128MiB (default 128MiB, at least 8MiB); a run that passes it is killed. cpu: the CPUs it may use (default 1).
The services of this node the function may reach, each on one tcp port the service declares. A link opens the way and nothing else: no connection value is put in the function's environment.

A proposal made with action_propose fills it in, so the owner's card says that the image is fetched with the credential and that Incus then keeps it with the image; a caller has no need to state it. x-arca-refusals.summary: The call would pass a cap, and nothing was written. scope says whose cap: tenant (the tenant's own caps) or node (the node's caps, its room for tenants, its service subnet, or a tenant's address block that something else has filled); a call in a tenant can be refused by either. limit names the cap: a count of instances, containers, virtual machines, CPUs, tenants or addresses, or an amount of memory or disk. have (in use), want (asked) and max (allowed) are there when known, in bytes for memory and disk and as a count for every other cap; with scope node they are the node's amounts, not the tenant's. proposeAgain: true means the refusal came from running an approved action: that approval is spent, so the action is proposed again once there is room.

The caller asked too often, or too much of its own already waits: a wait ends it. retryAfterSeconds is there when the wait is known; where room can also be made sooner (a waiting request is decided), it is the longest the wait can be. After the wait the same call is allowed again, with one exception: proposeAgain: true means the refusal came from running an approved action, whose approval is spent, so after the wait the action is proposed again and approved again.
One token recorded its thirty new action proposals of ten minutes. The same kind of refusal as rate, under the name it has always had. retryAfterSeconds is the wait until the window has a free place.

Eight action proposals already wait for the owner, from any token. The same kind of refusal as rate, under the name it has always had. It carries no field: room is made when one is approved or declined, or lapses fifteen minutes after it was made.
